signals.brief: A supply-chain threat wave is hitting developer and ML infrastructure at once. Black Lotus Labs details PoeLLM, malware that pulls its C&C IP from keywords hidden in a GitHub poem and targets exposed AI/open-source services (LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea) for crypto-mining and botnet growth. The GhostAction campaign pushed secret-stealing GitHub Actions workflows to 772 public repositories between Aug 31 and Sep 30, targeting 2,577 secrets including SSH keys and cloud credentials. Separately, a credential-stealing worm turned up in tensorlake's npm SDK 0.5.144, and CVE-2026-47483 in Nvidia's DCGM Exporter lets unauthenticated attackers flood endpoints and leak GPU telemetry from 12,000+ GPUs.
signals.headline: Supply-chain wave: GhostAction hits 772 repos, PoeLLM hides C&C in a poem, Nvidia DCGM CVE
signals.noahPrompt: GhostAction stole 2,577 secrets via GitHub Actions. Design a CI/CD hardening checklist (token scoping, action pinning, secret detection) that would have blunted this campaign, and explain how PoeLLM's dead-drop C&C changes your detection strategy.
